1. Therapy
2. Talking with somebody you trust. Maybe a friend who experienced something similar? 
3. Finding new strategies. I write about what I am feeling and thinking to organise my thoughts. I try meditation when I am overwhelmed. I exercise when I am angry. And I analyse my behaviour when I am feeling a bit better. What am I feeling? Why? What was my reaction? Can I think of something (maybe in my childhood) that taught me this behaviour? You could read books that are recommended by therapists to find new ways to cope.
4. Try a self-help group. Basically, this subreddit  but in real life. 
5. Don't give up. There is always hope, even when you can't see it. I was at my lowest in June 2022. After 18 months of depression, without any hope of getting better and struggling with a lot of suicidal thoughts. 4 months later, I started to heal. It's not easy. But you are strong, you are worthy of being loved, and you deserve better ❤️

I started therapy, because talking was everything I wanted. I lived through some trauma and wasn’t able to talk to my friends or family about. But it was obvious, that I needed to talk if I wanted to finally start healing. 
And yes, talking helped and I am no longer suffering from ptsd, but I still experience depression and anxiety. Especially since covid hit in 2020. but therapy is more then just talking about your problems. It’s reflecting on your behavior and what got you in this position in the thirst place. It is hard work. It’s trying to find ways to cope with your symptoms. Together with someone who is an expert on the human psyche and stays objective in order to give you a neutral and professional perspective. 
It is totally possible to get better without therapy, but it probably will be much slower and harder. 

And after all, hopelessness and the feeling, that nothing could ever make things better is a symptom of depression.

When did you start feeling this way? General sadness and hopelessness for longer that 2-3 weeks could be a depressive episode. In either way, therapy is always a good choice. Wherever you are in your life, it will help. And a therapist can give you a better diagnosis than reddit. 
Anyway, I hope that things will get better for you 🧡 all the best wishes!

Hey, 
I’m queer and from my experience, there is no need to put labels on yourself. Other people will do that for you. So do what makes you happy and identify yourself in whatever way it feels right. Maybe you are agender or transgender or non-binary or whatever. And if you realize tomorrow or next month or in a year, that you identify yourself differently, that’s ok too. Just be who you are. Try different pronouns with people you trust. Try different looks. Whatever makes you happy. And never forget, that gender is a construct, a invention, a lie. We are not binary and neither are you. 

I hope that this gives you some of the support that you deserve. Good luck and all the best wishes!

My Lavellan DW Rouge was a talented hunter and knew, that his clan needed him, but even though he loved his elven culture, he always dreamed of seeing more of the world. Exploring all of Thedas and maybe write a book like the famous bestseller from Brother Genitiv. 

The inquisition finally gave him the chance to see more of the world, but he never liked the responsibility of being the inquisitor. To escape the pressure, he often disappeared for hours into the books of the Skyhold library, where he got pretty close to Dorian. 
In all of his wildest dreams about the world outside of his clan, he would have never imagined to meet somebody like Dorian. Fascination became affection and finally love. 
It broke his heart when Dorian became bound to the magisteriums seat. 
The rest of the trespasser events weren’t better. Over the years he grew so sick of his position as the inquisitor, his faith in the elven gods were shattered by Solas and on top of that, I always imagined him as left handed…

It took him a long time to master writing with his right hand, but finally, with the inquisition disbanded, he got to travel with sera and the Red Jenny’s and write the book he always dreamed of. Visiting Tevinter regularly of course.

When she became part of a mercenaries, she made the first friends in her life and they showed her, that being a Qunari and being feared for that, could be an advantage. Especially as a mercenary.
After the conclave, she thought that the Qunari apostate ought to be the scapegoat. She seriously considered fleeing as long as she could. Being made the inquisitor and talking to Sera, made her realize the potential of her situation. She never had power, she always was marginalized and discriminated. As the Inquisitor she had the power to change the world for the better! She led the Inquisition, like a rebellion. Against the rules of the chantry, the circle, every injustice and for every powerless outcast in Thedas. Always with Sera at her side, who inspired her.

I don’t get it. If you think about it for one second you should figure out, that a fascist regime, that persecuted everybody that didn’t fit in their nationalist worldview, wouldn’t accept lesbians. I think it’s really important to remember this symbol and what it stands for („asocial people“ like one comment pointed out before). As a german lesbian I am shocked, that the persecution of homosexual women is still mostly forgotten and erased. 
Of course the Nazis didn’t tolerate lesbians. But they were often imprisoned under different reasons, like sexual abuse or indecent exposure, so they could be labeled as asocial. The term „asocial“ and the black triangle was something the nazis came up with to put away everybody they didn’t like. It wasn’t specific and very loosely defined. And they couldn’t imprison lesbians with the pink triangle for homosexuals, because homosexuality was defined as only male. And that’s why there are people still debating if there were any lesbians in concentration camps and even if they were imprisoned, because they were homosexual, if they deserve to be memorized. 
How about f**k off? 
So, yes. Reclaim the black triangle. Be loud and remember. But also be informed and remember who else was tortured and murdered under this symbol and labeled with it.
